data.outcome_summary: This OECD PISA 2022 results factsheet summarizes how 15-year-old students in Singapore performed in mathematics, reading, and science, and how results changed over time (notably 2018 to 2022 and comparisons to 2009 and 2012). It reports mean performance, trends, and proficiency distributions using PISA 2022 proficiency levels (e.g., Level 2 baseline and Level 5/6 top performers), with uncertainty shown via 95% confidence intervals. For Singapore, 92% of students reached at least Level 2 in mathematics (OECD average: 69%), 41% were top performers (Level 5/6), 89% reached Level 2+ in reading (OECD average: 74%), and 92% reached Level 2+ in science (OECD average: 76%). The factsheet also highlights within-country equity patterns (socio-economic gradients, gender differences, and immigrant background gaps) and contextualizes findings with school climate, belonging, safety, parental involvement, and system resources. It is descriptive and does not implement or evaluate machine-learning models, so no ML performance metrics or causal claims are made.
